sources.title: Comments on Kämmerer, et al. (2023) regarding RT-PCR Testing
sources.authors_or_institution: Fabio Franchi (Independent Researcher); Jerneja Tomsic (Researcher, City of Hope Comprehensive Cancer Center, Duarte, USA)
sources.why_relevant: Formal journal comment disputing that SARS-CoV-2 was properly isolated/purified: argues Koch's postulates require a "purified germ," which "was not available for COVID-19."
sources.quote: in order to test the first and the second of Koch's postulates, there must be both a purified germ and a specified disease, neither of which was available for COVID-19.

sources.title: Response to Comments on Kämmerer, et al. (2023) regarding RT-PCR Testing
sources.authors_or_institution: Ulrike Kämmerer, Sona Pekova, Rainer J. Klement, Rogier Louwen, Pieter Borger, Klaus Steger (Universitätsklinikum Würzburg)
sources.why_relevant: Formal journal reply defending standard cell-culture isolation of SARS-CoV-2 and addressing the Koch's-postulates/purification objection raised in the comment.
sources.quote: They point to the lack of a specific definition of COVID-19 disease and conclude that, in order to test the first and the second of Koch's postulates, there must be both a purified germ and a specified disease, neither of which was available for COVID-19. In reply, we address two questions they did not ask: ... 2. Are Koch's postulates valid for viruses?

notes: Ten English searches were run (isolation dispute/critique/reply, cell culture, Koch's postulates, Europe PMC). Opened peer-reviewed sources surfaced successful isolation reports and technical culture-optimization papers, plus the IJVTPR comment/reply exchange below (primarily RT-PCR framing, with an isolation/purification point via Koch's postulates). No other peer-reviewed isolation/culture-method dispute with a published reply was located; broader "not isolated" claims appear in non-peer-reviewed blogs/FOI/fact-checks, which are excluded. Neither source duplicates SOURCES.json (Harcourt CDC EID, Sarkale IJMR, Araujo, Kim PHRP).
